PRIVACY NOTICE

Clear about what
we collect and why.

Last updated 8 October 2026. This notice covers the Fabrication Intelligence pilot website, the shop, contact messages, quote requests and client or manufacturer accounts.

What we collect

When you submit a request, we may collect your name, email, company, project details, product requirements, timing, destination and an optional drawing. Account users also provide login details and a client or manufacturer profile. Manufacturer applicants may provide company capabilities, certifications and website information. Product order requests also include recipient and billing details, delivery address, phone, selected products, quantities and acceptance of the order process. When you use the contact form, we collect your name, email, message and any product you mention.

Why we use it

We use this information to understand and respond to sourcing requests, prepare comparable quote options, operate accounts, review manufacturer applications, protect private files and improve the pilot.

Where it is stored

Website source code is stored in GitHub and the website is hosted through Vercel and GitHub Pages. Personal account and request data is stored in Supabase, not in the public source repository. Account, request and private upload data is handled through Supabase. Passwords are handled by Supabase Auth and are not visible to the Fabrication Intelligence team. Private drawings and supplier files are not public. When you submit a quote request or the feedback form, or send a message through the contact form, the details (but not any drawing) are also emailed to the FI team through FormSubmit so we can reply quickly.

Who can access it

Approved FI team accounts can access quote requests and files needed to operate the service. Clients can access only requests linked to their own signed-in account. Manufacturer applicants can access only their own application; approval status is controlled separately by FI. Approved supplier workspaces remain invitation-only.

Payments and marketing

A product can only be bought online once we mark it live in the shop. When you buy one, checkout happens on Shopify’s or Stripe’s own pages and your card details go to them, not to us. We receive your order details, such as your name, email and delivery address, so we can fulfil the order. For the warehouse order service, FI stores provider payment references, amounts, refunds and disputes, supplier source links, purchase instructions, inspection evidence and both shipment legs. Card numbers and CVCs are not stored by FI. Delivery details are shared with the warehouse and delivery carrier when needed; suppliers receive the FI warehouse destination. Checkout for this service stays disabled until activated by FI. We do not sell your personal information. We do not add you to marketing messages merely because you submitted a request or placed an order.

Retention and your choices

We keep pilot records only for as long as reasonably needed to respond, operate the service and document the project. To ask for access, correction or deletion, email fabricationintelligence@gmail.com. Some records may need to be retained where required by law or legitimate project administration.

Optional website analytics

Google Analytics is being prepared and is not yet active. When enabled, it will run only on public pages after you choose Allow analytics. It uses cookies to measure page visits, approved clicks and successful enquiries. We do not send form contents, names, email addresses, customer IDs, payment details, URL query strings or account and order pages through this integration. Google still processes technical data, including device/browser information and network information, to provide analytics.

Analytics consent is stored in this browser, and analytics cookies are set with a 90-day expiry. You can decline without losing access to forms or accounts. Once analytics is enabled, use Analytics choices in the footer to change your decision. Declining stops new tracking and clears this site's analytics cookies; it does not automatically delete data already sent to Google. Read how Google uses information from sites that use its services. Message experiments are deferred; any future experiment labels will describe the message shown, not identify you.

Pilot status

This is a student-led pilot, not a final automated marketplace. The service may change as the team learns from early users. Material privacy changes will be reflected on this page.
